review_scope: Independent risk-weighted semantic spot checks with bounded follow-up repairs. This is not a proof of correctness for every knowl or an estimate of corpus error prevalence.

selection.selection: 8 new foundations, 8 highest direct-dependent hubs, 13 repaired-boundary definitions, 12 largest prerequisite removals (ties by dependent count/ID), 7 remaining controls sampled with seed 20260905. Risk-weighted sample; not an estimate of corpus error prevalence.

reviews.rationale: The body correctly defines a permutation as a bijection [n] to itself, including the n=0 convention and one-line notation. Both prerequisites are directly used; the function prerequisite is transitively covered by bijective-function. No missing or reversed dependency was found.
reviews.resolution: confirmed; related prerequisite corrections incorporated where noted

reviews.rationale: The inversion definition and (-1)^inv formula are correct, including the empty permutation. finite-permutation already supplies n in N and [n], so natural-numbers is a redundant direct prerequisite under transitive coverage; removing it leaves the needed concept. The remaining prerequisite is correctly oriented.
reviews.resolution: corrected

reviews.rationale: The definition agrees with the standard Noetherian-local definition: the maximal ideal has a minimal generating number equal to dim(R), equivalently dim_k(m/m^2)=dim(R). The cited Stacks definition states exactly this (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02IR). Locality, Noetherianity, Krull dimension, the residue field, quotient module, vector-space structure, and the basis/dimension notion all support the displayed definition; no dependency is missing or reversed.
reviews.resolution: confirmed; related prerequisite corrections incorporated where noted

reviews.rationale: The body correctly says locally Noetherian with all stalks regular local, and correctly spells out affine Noetherian neighborhoods. This is equivalent to the Stacks definition (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02IR), which gives the same locally Noetherian/stalk characterization. locally-ringed-space is already part of the scheme prerequisite and is therefore redundant; the remaining dependencies are correctly oriented.
reviews.resolution: corrected

reviews.rationale: The body correctly defines X times_S Spec(overline{kappa(s)}) and distinguishes it from the ordinary residue-field fiber. A choice of algebraic closure together with the inclusion kappa(s) into it gives the stated geometric point. morphism-of-schemes, fiber-product, residue-field, and algebraic-closure are needed. scheme-over-a-base merely repackages the already-given morphism f:X to S and is redundant; the standard Stacks discussion confirms geometric fibers are formed by such base changes (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/038S).
reviews.resolution: corrected

reviews.rationale: The C1 map and action laws are a correct global flow definition; phi_{-t} is the inverse of phi_t by the laws, and is C1 because it is another time map. The real line, composition, manifold charts, and differentiability language are all used. The local-flow distinction is accurate. No missing, irrelevant, or reversed prerequisite was found.
reviews.resolution: confirmed; related prerequisite corrections incorporated where noted

reviews.rationale: The set of tangent vectors satisfying g_x(v,v)=1 is the correct unit tangent bundle, and the fiber description follows from the Riemannian metric. The separate norm prerequisite is redundant because the Riemannian-manifold body already defines the metric-induced length used here. The other two prerequisites are needed and correctly oriented.
reviews.resolution: corrected

reviews.rationale: The geodesic equation nabla_{dot gamma} dot gamma=0 is correct, and metric compatibility implies constant speed. The initial-value existence and uniqueness statement is the standard local ODE result for a smooth Riemannian manifold and its Levi-Civita connection; maximal extension and the unit-speed specialization are correctly stated. All three prerequisites are used and correctly oriented.
reviews.resolution: confirmed; related prerequisite corrections incorporated where noted

content_corrections.after: For the reversed curve \(\bar\gamma(t)=\gamma(1-t)\), uniqueness of horizontal lifts gives a diffeomorphism \(P_\gamma:D_\gamma\to D_{\bar\gamma}\) with inverse \(P_{\bar\gamma}\). It is a diffeomorphism between the entire fibers when lifts exist throughout \([0,1]\) for every initial point in both directions. This holds for a complete connection. Forward existence alone need not give surjectivity.
content_corrections.rationale: Forward-complete flow can have a proper image (for example y′=-y³). Both forward and reverse domains are needed for a whole-fiber diffeomorphism.

content_corrections.before: On a complex line bundle with connection given locally by a 1-form \(A\), parallel transport along \(\gamma\) multiplies a vector in the fiber by a phase factor determined by integrating \(A\) along \(\gamma\) (after choosing a local trivialization).
content_corrections.after: In a trivialization along \(\gamma\) where a complex line-bundle connection is \(\nabla=d+A\), parallel transport multiplies the fiber coordinate by \(\exp(-\int_\gamma A)\). For a Hermitian connection in a unitary frame, \(A\) is imaginary-valued and this multiplier is a phase. A general complex connection can also change its magnitude.
content_corrections.rationale: The sign follows from the parallel ODE. A phase requires a Hermitian connection and unitary frame; general complex connections need not preserve norm.
